The Faster Labor Contracts Act (S.844) forces employers to bargain within 10 days post-unionization and imposes binding arbitration after 120 days. While streamlining negotiations sounds efficient, Section 3(C) creates a new federal arbitration bureaucracy to resolve disputes - expanding DOL's role rather than empowering private-sector solutions.

The Teamsters' cheerleading proves unions see this as a power grab to bypass tough negotiations. Real reform would let workers and employers hash out terms without D.C. mediators dictating wage benchmarks.

This isn’t “fair treatment” - it’s federally mandated contract terms disguised as labor rights.
